books.title: Chapter I: My Childhood
books.description:
I grew up an ordinary American kid — a little spoiled, if I'm honest. My worries were small
ones: getting through high school, being tongue-tied around girls, the everyday stuff of being
a teenager. I was decent at sports, and as my confidence grew, the shyness faded — until one
girlfriend wasn't enough for me, and I cheated. I didn't know it then, but the seeds of a
selfish heart were already showing.

books.title: Chapter II: There Were Signs
books.description:
The truth is, I was selfish — not loudly, where everyone could see it, but quietly and on
purpose. I learned how to arrange things so they benefited me while nobody noticed; sometimes
it even made me look like the one making the sacrifice. I never let a chance like that pass.
I was self-seeking to the core. It's a dark thing to admit, and it still makes me emotional to
think about the people I hurt — people who never deserved it. I am sorry. Truly sorry.

books.title: Chapter III: What Happened
books.description:
Then life started taking people. Between my teens and adulthood, I lost my dad and my brother,
six years apart — and in between, I spent four years in the Marine Corps. In my immature mind,
drinking felt almost necessary to carry all that. So I drank, and then I reached for more, and
more kept costing more. The consequences piled up, and my world grew hopeless, dark, and
helpless. That went on into my thirties: relationship to relationship, rehab to rehab, until
things got so bad there was no denying it anymore. I had a real problem — and it had me.

books.title: Chapter IV: Jesus Set Me Free
books.description:
For years, alcohol owned me. I didn't drink to celebrate; I drank to disappear. I went through
rehab more times than I can count — every time swearing I was done, every time proving I
wasn't. I was a slave, and I knew it.

Then one night, with nothing left — no pride, no plan — I cried out to God. It wasn't a pretty
prayer. It was just one word: help.

And He answered — not with lightning, but with freedom. Day by day the chains came off, and the
cravings that used to shout started to lose their voice.

Jesus said, "If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." That's John 8:36. It's not a
slogan to me. It's my life.

By God's grace, I'm eight years sober now. Not because I'm strong — because He is faithful.

books.title: Chapter V: Since Then
books.description:
Two years ago, I ended this page by saying I would add to the story as the Lord gave it to me.
He has been giving ever since.

He restored my home. He gave me back my son Jude after years apart — years I believed were gone
for good.

And He put a work in my hands. By day, I help families sort out their student loans. Around
that day job, the Lord has had me building TruVINE, and a home for His Word called Word of God
Risen — where anyone can read the Bible and hear it read out loud, free: no account, no
password. I had Grandpa Teddy read the whole Bible out loud, in one trusted voice, so anybody,
anywhere, could hear all of it.

Now people in places I may never visit are opening the Word, and churches — like our brothers
and sisters in Bacong, in the Philippines — are carrying it to their congregations. We plant.
We water. God gives the increase.

None of this is about me. The seeking never starts with the created thing, but with the Creator.
I sought Him because He sought me first.

And if He did it for me, He can do it for you. Don't give up.

— Jason
